newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua telephone sale likely delayed until 1998.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua telephone sale likely delayed until 1998.

text.p: The much-delayed partial sale of Nicaragua's state telephone company Enitel almost certainly will not happen in 1997 and likely will take place in mid-1998, Enitel President Pablo Ayon said on Wednesday.

"It's almost impossible to hold the sale this year for time reasons. I think if everything goes well, and the government authorizes the process, it could take place in one and a half years, or in the middle of the next year," Ayon told reporters.
Nicaragua has planned to sell 40 percent of the Empresa Nicaraguense de Telecomunicaciones (Enitel) for two years, but repeatedly has postponed its sale.
There were last-minute postponements last year on July 27 and October 3, and the government also postponed the awarding of a concession that had been scheduled for the end of March.

Ayon said the new government of President Arnoldo Aleman, which took power on January 10, was reviewing the terms of the planned sale of Enitel. Those terms were formulated by the previous government of President Violeta Chamorro.

He said officials first must qualify new companies seeking to bid for Enitel and then give the companies at least three months to examine the terms of the sale, meaning the probability of Nicaragua being ready to sell Enitel in 1997 was almost zero.

Aleman has set three basic conditions for the sale of Enitel: it must offer true economic benefits to Nicaragua; the state must maintain enough control of Enitel to guarantee good service and reasonable prices; and the buying company must guarantee sufficient technological development and added telephones lines.
"If no one offers the conditions mentioned by the president as a base, then we will not sell it and we will continue as we are," Ayon said.
Ayon said that Nicaragua should receive more than $100 million for 40 percent of Enitel.
